title: CHAPTER FIFTEEN. On the intellect of God; definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): But ye formal consists in ye position belonging toward ye most supereminent mode belonging toward spiritual life by means belonging toward that same which God most perfectly understands all things. namely God's highest perfection — the material in this attribute also stands as ye same as in ye others. Intellect, so called by means belonging toward ye Latins out from inter plus lego, by means belonging toward force belonging toward etymology notes ye power, act, plus habit by means belonging toward that same which we know so as to have choice between this plus that same — that same which stands as to know so as to discern. by means belonging toward that same which He distinctly, most inwardly, plus most perfectly knows all plus each things that same which in any way are, were, will be, or can be, plus ye order, connection, plus various respects belonging toward all plus each among themselves that same which they have plus can have, plus their opposites — the intellect belonging toward God stands as His highest perfection. On ye intellect belonging toward God. CHAPTER FIFTEEN.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER FIFTEEN. On the intellect of God.

The intellect of God is His highest perfection, by which He distinctly, most inwardly, and most perfectly knows all and each things which in any way are, were, will be, or can be, and the order, connection, and various respects of all and each among themselves which they have and can have, and their opposites.

Intellect, so called by the Latins from inter and lego, by force of etymology notes the power, act, and habit by which we know so as to have choice between this and that — which is to know so as to discern. The material in this attribute also is the same as in the others, namely God's highest perfection. But the formal consists in the position of the most supereminent mode of spiritual life by which God most perfectly understands all things.
source_text: CAPUT DECIMUMQUINTUM, De intellectu Dei. Intellectus Dei est summa illius perfectio, qua omnia et singula, quae quomodocunque sunt, fuerunt, erunt, esse possunt, omniumque et singulorum inter se ordinem, connexionem, variosque respectus quos habent et habere possunt, eorumque opposita, distincte, penitisime, perfectissimeque cognoscit. Intellectus, ab inter et lego Latinis dictus, vi etymi notat potentiam, actum et habitum, quo novimus ita ut delectum habeamus inter hoc et aliud, quod est cognoscere ut dignoscas. Materiale quidem etiam in hoc attributo idem est quod in aliis, summa nempe Dei perfectio. Formale vero est in positione modi spiritualis vitae supereminentissimi, quo Deus omnia perfectissime intelligit.
